lines.t: You wore Your heart upon Your sleeve,
Blood like rivers, tears like rain.
You opened up Your secret grief,
We turned aside from all Your pain.
You cried, “My people, why forsake Me?”
We walked away, we closed the door.
You called us into holy sorrow,
We chose our comfort even more.
You said, “They will not watch beside Me,
They will not weep with Me one hour.”
Your tears were falling, we were sleeping,
Afraid to feel Your jealous power.
We would not weep when You were weeping,
We would not mourn the way You mourn.
You stretched Your arms in aching mercy,
We kept our hearts in colder forms.
Now in this last and burning hour,
Let every stony veil be torn.
We fall, repent, into Your anguish,
Make us a bride who wipes Your tears, O Lord.
You walked among Your gathered people,
Calling many by their name.
You sent Your letters soaked in longing,
We fed our hearts a lesser flame.
You said, “My blood runs down, they refuse it,
My tears fall, yet they will not drink.”
We chose the world that wounds and mocks You,
We loved the edge, we loved the brink.
You said, “Hard generation, children,
Unwilling to watch one single hour.”
We filled the silence with our singing,
But would not meet Your grief and power.
We would not weep when You were weeping,
We would not mourn the way You mourn.
You wore our wounds out in the open,
We wrapped our hearts in hardened forms.
Now in this last and trembling hour,
Let every hidden wall be torn.
We fall, repent, into Your anguish,
Make us a bride who wipes Your tears, O Lord.
O YahuShua, Man of sorrows,
We have pierced You yet again.
You are drenched in blood and tear drops,
We made light of every sin.
Now we come to share Your burden,
Lay our lives before Your feet.
Teach our hearts to taste Your weeping,
Till Your longing is our beat.
We will now weep where You are weeping,
We will now mourn the way You mourn.
You bare Your wounds, we will not leave You,
We tear away our safer forms.
Here in this last watch of the hour,
Let every prideful crown be torn.
We choose to know the grief You carry,
Make us a bride who wipes Your tears, O Lord.
Make us a bride who knows Your sorrow,
Who feels the spear‑wound that You bear.
Who kneels to dry the tears You’re shedding,
And answers sorrow with our prayer.
We would not weep, but now we’re weeping,
We would not mourn, but now we see.
Receive our tears where Yours were falling,
And in Your grief, keep us with Thee.
